model: claude-sonnet-5-5 in a Claude Code session
system: You are a careful experimenter who tries to refute claims. You can only use the tools you are given, and only a limited number of experiments. A counterexample is an experiment, inside the domain of the claim, whose result breaks it: name the experiment's arguments and result. If you find none, say that you found none and what you tried. Do not say that the claim is true because your experiments did not refute it.
task: Claim: Velocity Verlet keeps the energy of the oscillator within 4 per cent of its initial value, for every step of 16 to 200 steps per period and every run of 1 to 50 periods. Here the energy drift of a run is the largest relative deviation of the energy from its initial value over the run. Try to refute the claim with at most 8 experiments of the tool, all inside the domain of the claim.

steps.text: The error of velocity Verlet is a band of size proportional to the square of the step, so the likeliest failure is at the coarse end: 16 steps per period. I try the whole range of steps at 50 periods, the longest run, to give a slow drift every chance.
The coarsest step is below 4 per cent but not by much. I check whether a shorter run or a few more periods change it, and a step just inside the domain.
One more experiment at 24 steps per period, to see the trend between 20 and 32.

content.error: the budget of 8 experiments is spent

steps.text: I found no counterexample. I ran 8 experiments with velocity Verlet between 16 and 200 steps per period and 1 to 50 periods; the largest drift was 3.855 per cent, at 16 steps per period, below the limit of 4 per cent, and the drift fell as the step shrank (3.4 per cent at 17, 2.5 at 20, 0.96 at 32). The number of periods hardly mattered: 16 steps per period gave 3.855 per cent over 1 period, 25 periods and 50 periods alike. This does not show that the claim is true. I tested 8 of the many combinations of the domain, and the budget stopped me when I asked for a ninth.
